learningObjective: Reason about executing a single model across heterogeneous devices (CPU + GPU + specialized accelerator) coordinated by a runtime.
stem: Which statements about heterogeneous execution (a single model spanning CPU + GPU or CPU + NPU) are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A partitioning pass typically groups ops into 'subgraphs' assigned to one device each, minimizing cross-device edges; the runtime executes each subgraph on its device and inserts transfer ops between them.

Cross-device edges are essentially free on modern PCIe 4.0 and NVLink; therefore the partitioning cost model can ignore transfer cost and choose the fastest device for each op independently, giving a partition that is optimal by construction.

Heterogeneous execution requires all devices to share a unified virtual memory space with cache coherence; without hardware support such as CXL, correct execution is impossible on machines with discrete GPUs.

Some accelerators (NPUs) have restricted op coverage; the runtime must decide, on a per-op basis, whether the op runs on the NPU (fast for supported ops) or falls back to CPU/GPU (slower but universal), and the partitioning cost model must model this asymmetry.

explanation: A: subgraph partitioning + inserted transfers is the standard technique (ONNX Runtime execution providers, OpenVINO plugins). D: NPU-style accelerators support a subset of ops; the compiler must route unsupported ops elsewhere. C is wrong: heterogeneous execution works fine on discrete GPUs without hardware cache coherence, via explicit transfers. B is wrong: PCIe/NVLink transfers are far from free (microseconds to milliseconds for large tensors) and per-op transfer plus synchronization cost is a first-order concern in the partition cost model.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: cross-device transfer and synchronization cost is significant and cannot be ignored.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: cache coherence is not required; explicit transfer suffices.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: NPU op-coverage asymmetry is a real constraint.

assumptions: The runtime supports partitioning into per-device subgraphs and inserting explicit transfers.
nonImplications: Does not imply hardware coherence (CXL, unified memory) is never useful; it does reduce programming complexity, but is not required.
Does not imply the coarsest partition is always best; extreme coarsening may under-utilize a fast device.

distractorRationales.C: Overstates the hardware requirement for heterogeneous execution.

sourceRefs.locator: ONNX Runtime execution providers and subgraph partitioning

performanceClaim.scope: Heterogeneous execution with partitioned subgraphs and explicit device transfers
